known_information: The reporter supplies EDID model GSM4B6B, connection paths, recovery sequence and a diagnostic archive.
The supplied Power Display log shows capability probing, two retries and unavailable capabilities; later entries show GSM4B6B skipped by the blacklist.
The reporter says local blacklist patching resolves the monitor loss; this is reporter validation, not an independent hardware test.
issue_context.analysis: A model-specific blacklist entry reuses the established compatibility mitigation and avoids probing this reported hardware. The logs support probe/exclusion behavior, not a definitive diagnosis of the internal scaler or kernel watchdog. A configurable opt-out is a separate broader feature and should not expand the narrow fix.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report, current discussion, labels, assignees and linked-work timeline.
Read BuiltInMonitorBlacklist.json: it already includes LTM2C02 and GSM7714, but not GSM4B6B.
Read MonitorBlacklistService: exclusions match normalized model EDID identifiers before discovery; existing tests cover the mechanism.
Read related issue 47968; the older model and kernel failure are distinct, so do not mark this exact model handled by that issue.
Reassessed the complete current issue discussion and timeline, including the latest maintainer labels. Label changes alone do not satisfy unanswered evidence requests or prove a repair.
issue_context.summary: LG L194W capability probes correlate with monitor loss; a model-level exclusion is a narrowly supported mitigation.

confidence.rationale: The archive and existing exclusion mechanism strongly support the mitigation, but hardware behavior and the exact underlying firmware/driver failure are not independently reproduced.

Verify the exclusion is applied before capability requests; keep user-configurable policy out of this patch.
